TÜRKİYE · DAY-END SCORECARD · 6 November 2026
Yesterday the day-ahead price ran from its floor at 04:00 to its ceiling at 17:00.

🎯 Price swing: 2,500 TL/MWh between the floor and the ceiling.

📊 The day's generation mix (EPİAŞ):
🌞 Solar 6.3% (licensed 0.9% + unlicensed 5.4%)
💧 Hydro (dams + rivers) 28.5%
🍃 Wind 15.1%
🔥 Natural gas only 12.6%
🌱 Total renewables 55.0% — all fossil 45.0%

📉 The price (MCP, Market Clearing Price):
🌙 02:00–04:00 → 2,000 TL/MWh, the floor of the day, with demand at 32,342 MWh at 04:00
🌙 17:00–18:00 → 4,500 TL/MWh, the ceiling of the day, with demand at 46,932 MWh at 17:00
Daily average 3,214 TL/MWh.

From 11:00 to 17:00, the first hour of the ceiling run, demand barely moved, down 176 MWh. Solar (licensed + unlicensed) fell 9,078 MWh, hydro, wind and other renewables added 5,243 MWh and fossil plants added 3,661 MWh.

⚡ Balancing cost 9,075,289 TL, measured as value against the day-ahead price. Constraint-coded instructions made up 841 MWh of the 15,672 MWh instructed in both directions. The hour with the largest cost was 10:00, with 1,512 MWh of up-regulation. On the published supply curve, buying that volume in the day-ahead market would have lifted the clearing price to 3,967 TL/MWh, below that hour's SMP (System Marginal Price).

📆 Versus 5 November: the daily average was 2,729 TL/MWh and the floor 500 TL/MWh at 04:00, on a day with more wind than 6 November.
📆 Versus 30 October, the same weekday one week earlier: the daily average was 3,487 TL/MWh and the floor 2,501 TL/MWh at 02:00–03:00, on a day with less wind than 6 November.

💡 What it means:
A first reading: the climb in the day-ahead price from 07:00 to 08:00 is consistent with the morning demand ramp. Consumption rose 6,811 MWh in that hour, more than solar (licensed + unlicensed) and hydro, wind and other renewables added between them, so what fossil plants had left to cover, consumption minus those renewables, grew 1,893 MWh.

İlk okuma: gün öncesi fiyatının 07:00'den 08:00'e tırmanışı sabah tüketim rampasıyla tutarlı. Yesterday the balancing price sat above the day-ahead price in most hours.

🌙 18:00 → 4,150 TL/MWh, the ceiling of the day, with demand at 46,911 MWh

Between 11:00, the solar peak, and the 18:00 ceiling, demand rose 902 MWh and solar (licensed + unlicensed) fell 9,904 MWh. Over the same hours hydro, wind and other renewables added 5,761 MWh and fossil plants 4,856 MWh.

⚡ Balancing cost 8,316,707 TL, measured as value against the day-ahead price. Of 13,864 MWh of instructed volume, 577 MWh carried a constraint code. In Türkiye, how deep the day-ahead price falls at night follows what fossil plants have left to cover, not demand. TÜRKİYE · DAY-END SCORECARD · 23 October 2026
Yesterday the day-ahead price held its floor from 12:00 to 12:59, then ramped.

🎯 Duck curve: the price took 4 hours to climb from the end of its floor to the ceiling.

📊 The day's generation mix (EPİAŞ):
🌞 Solar 14.8% (licensed 3.0% + unlicensed 11.8%)
💧 Hydro (dams + rivers) 23.8%
🍃 Wind 4.8%
🔥 Natural gas only 15.6%
🌱 Total renewables 48.8% — all fossil 51.2%

📉 The price (MCP, Market Clearing Price):
🌞 12:00 → 250 TL/MWh, the floor of the day, with solar at 19,455 MWh
🌙 17:00–19:00 → 4,500 TL/MWh, the ceiling of the day, with demand at 43,660 MWh in its first hour
Daily average 3,242 TL/MWh.

Between 11:00 and 17:00, the first hour of the ceiling run, demand fell 301 MWh and solar (licensed + unlicensed) fell 18,698 MWh. Over the same hours hydro, wind and other renewables added 8,065 MWh and fossil plants added 10,249 MWh.

⚡ Balancing cost 6,173,538 TL, measured as value against the day-ahead price. Of 38,588 MWh of instructed volume, 14,757 MWh was constraint-coded. The largest hourly cost, 2,534,672 TL, came at 15:00, when down-regulation was far more than up-regulation: surplus energy that real time did not need, which day-ahead buying cannot close.

📆 Versus 22 October 2026: daily average 3,186 TL/MWh, floor 300 TL/MWh at 12:00.
📆 Versus 16 October 2026, the same weekday one week earlier: daily average 2,989 TL/MWh, 2,274 TL/MWh at 12:00 and 2,300 TL/MWh at 02:00–04:00, 13:00 and 23:00.

💡 What it means:
In Türkiye, hydro, wind and other renewables rise and fall with the day-ahead price across a day of weak wind. Their output on 23 October bottomed out at 7,327 MWh at 12:00, the hour of the price floor, then climbed to 17,796 MWh at 18:00, with the price held at its ceiling. On 22 October output traced the same path, rising from 8,528 MWh at the 12:00 floor into the 17:00–19:00 ceiling run.

Source: EPİAŞ Transparency Platform, 23 October 2026 (retrieved 24 October 2026, 12:33 UTC+3)
